Q386.L1t: The passage is a short piece of writing about Nelson Mandela, the South African leader who became famous around the world.
Q386.L2t: The passage is organized as a numbered list of four separate facts about Mandela's habits, name, release and studies.
Q386.L3t: The passage opens by saying that many details of his life were public knowledge, and then introduces four things readers may not have known, which it presents as a list of lesser-known facts.
Q386.L4t: The passage is mainly about little-known facts concerning Mandela that most people have not heard before.
Q386.L2f: The passage says Mandela received his English name from a teacher at a Methodist primary school in Qunu when he was nine years old, and that he never used his original name again.
Q386.L3f: The passage is mostly built around his 27 years behind bars, and the facts it lists, such as exercising each morning and finishing his law degree, are mainly there to show how he spent that time.
Q386.L4f: The passage is mainly about what Mandela's life was like while he was held in prison.

Q837.L1t: The passage reports a US study that compares how boys are educated in single-sex schools and in mixed schools.
Q837.L2t: The study was written by Abigail James of the University of Virginia, and it argues that boys in single-sex schools feel less pressure to follow a stereotype of masculinity.
Q837.L3t: James says that in single-sex schools teachers can adjust lessons to boys' learning style, for example by letting them move around the classroom and compete in teams, and by using themes and characters that appeal to boys.
Q837.L4t: According to James, single-sex schools let teachers fit their teaching to the way boys learn best.
Q837.L2f: The study found that boys in mixed schools generally do better than boys in single-sex schools in speaking and reading, which is why mixed teaching has long been favoured.
Q837.L3f: James argues that without girls in the room boys are less distracted and daydream less, and that this lets them concentrate fully on what is being taught.
Q837.L4f: According to James, the advantage of single-sex schools is that boys can concentrate on lessons without being absent-minded.

Q802.L1t: The passage is a news-style feature about a man in Maryland who gathers secrets that strangers send to him.
Q802.L2t: Frank Warren started PostSecret as an art project ten years ago, and people began sending him postcards, objects and emails with their secrets written on them.
Q802.L3t: Warren says he was struggling with secrets in his own life, and he describes PostSecret as a safe place where others could share theirs, a space he needed as much as they did.
Q802.L4t: Warren created PostSecret to give people a safe place where they could share their secrets.
Q802.L2f: Warren has been choosing ten secrets every Sunday for the past ten years, and he posts them on the website only after checking each one with his wife.
Q802.L3f: Warren says he began the project because he wanted material for books, and each time he gathered enough secrets he turned them into a new volume to publish.
Q802.L4f: Warren created PostSecret in order to collect more material for his series of books.
